It has a lot of issues that are getting somewhat addressed as time goes on, and I look forward to the modding scene taking off more strongly as most issues from all the fallout games get handled there eventually. The biggest issue from the outside is that a lot of fallout 4's best content is for a dumb reason actually largely hidden.

There's hundreds of small stories to find the results of around the place, there's the whole curie quest line you can just straight up miss if you move even a little too quickly, there's a load of quest lines that have entire equipment sets and voiced dialogue that just don't happen if you leave a room too fast or talk to the people you think are important and move on.

The voiced main characters, the dialogue being a straight line dressed up in a choose your own response system, the perk system being too gamey and build focused, the player owned settlements having no flavor to them and little effect on the world outside story arcs tangentially in certain circumstances. A lot of stuff didn't sit well with me even if they provided just enough buoyancy to keep the game afloat.

I'm hoping modding fills in the gaps, I know I should expect that of the developer but they've delivered a lot even if it isn't exactly what I would want it to be, that stuff costed even if it was flawed. And it was enough to get me into the game, I hope the oncoming DLC expands on the functionality more, so the modding scene can use that functionality to create a load of content.

It seems to happen a lot. Take a front page post, post it anywhere else, that post is now on the front page too. Or they'll do it the next day. I don't typically downvote it, but fuck it's annoying seeing the same shit posted everywhere.

I don't know, for me it depends a lot on the size of the subs. This post, for example, could have gone in /v/Technology or /v/Politics. They're both big subs, so I just picked the one that I felt was most relevant (/v/technology), with the assumption that may people are subbed to both.

But with smaller subs, I don't mind posting to the smaller sub and then cross-posting to the larger one. For example, I post regularly in small gaming subs to try to keep them moving. When I see something that might be of interest to /v/gaming's community, I'll cross-post it there. The small sub gets a bit of exposure, and /v/gaming gets content that might interest them.
